title: Work, Kids and Home: How to Lose Weight When You Really Don't Have Time
intro: If you feel you have no time at all for yourself, you're not alone. You can still lose weight, as long as you focus on a few small habits that fit into your life right now.

sections.p: Don't try to change everything at once. Pick two or three things, for example cutting down on sweet drinks, adding protein and walking. Once they become routine, then add more.
No need to cook two kinds of dishes. Cook the usual family menu, just change your own plate. More vegetables and lauk, moderate rice. Cook a bit extra tonight for tomorrow's packed lunch.

sections.h: Watch out for your kids' leftovers
sections.p: Finishing your kids' leftover rice and nuggets looks small, but if it happens every day it can add up. Keep the leftovers for tomorrow or dish out less on your kids' plates. Eat when you actually sit down to eat.

Exercise doesn't have to be at the gym. Play catching, walk to the park, or do a 10-minute workout in the living room with your kids joining in. Added up, small movements throughout the week really help.

sections.h: Ask for help and protect your sleep
sections.p: Talk to your spouse about sharing house chores, even if it's just 2-3 times a week. Enough sleep helps control appetite and energy. You don't have to do everything alone.

action: Write down 2 habits you want to focus on this week and stick them on the fridge.
Cook one extra portion tonight to use as tomorrow's packed lunch.
Prepare your own plate first before you start feeding your kids, so you don't end up eating only leftovers.
Do a 10-minute workout in the living room with your kids 3 times this week.
Ask your spouse to take over one night-time chore so you can sleep earlier once a week.
myth: Many people believe you need to exercise for an hour every day to lose weight. Actually, short 10-20 minute sessions done consistently, plus good eating habits, are enough to start seeing changes.

faq.q: Do I need to cook different food for myself?
faq.a: No need. Eat the same menu as your family, just change the portion. Add vegetables, take a protein lauk, and keep the rice moderate.

faq.q: When is the best time to exercise if I have young kids?
faq.a: The best time is the time you can repeat. Some choose early morning before the kids wake up, some choose after the kids are asleep. Try a few timings and stick with the one that suits you best.

faq.q: I always eat dinner late because I settle the kids first. What should I do?
faq.a: Have a protein snack in the afternoon, for example a boiled egg or yogurt, so you don't get too hungry. When you eat dinner late, take a moderate portion and more vegetables.
